To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a method to predict driver intent using recurrent neural networks combined a mixture density network that is able to capture uncertainty and predict multiple modes of vehicle trajectories at an intersection.

(1) a recurrent neural network with a mixture density output layer can be used for trajectory prediction at urban intersections; (2) the model's performance is improved when the input is augmented with a map based representation of the intersection; (3) clustering the multi-modal output of the network improves the accuracy of the prediction.
we present a method for driver intention and trajectory prediction that can be applied to urban intersections with no traffic signals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (1) a novel dataset of vehicle trajectories at intersections; (2) a multi modal trajectory prediction method; (3) a method for consolidating the multi modal output into a set of possible future paths; (4) an evaluation methodology for trajectory prediction; and (5) a demonstration of the generalizability of the proposed method to a real world dataset.
the development of a novel method for predicting the intentions and future trajectories of drivers at urban intersections.
understanding the intentions of drivers and the paths they will take in urban intersections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is able to predict driver intent with an accuracy of 90% at a 3 second prediction window.
the model is a strong predictor of driver behavior at urban intersections and is able to capture the multi modality that is a hallmark of driver behavior.
the method is capable of accurately predicting the future trajectories of vehicles at urban intersections with high uncertainty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method can be used as a tool to help predict driver intent at intersections.
the proposed model outperforms the baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness.
our model is able to predict driver intent and paths in a real world setting with a high degree of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method presented is able to predict a diverse set of possible paths, which are consistent with the actual paths taken by the vehicles in the real world dataset.

we are able to capture the multi modal nature and uncertainty of the prediction problem, and we are able to do this without the requirement of a large amount of data, or the need for hand engineered features.

a recurrent neural network based trajectory prediction method can successfully predict the path of vehicles at urban intersections with high probability, even when the vehicle is not visible in the immediate past.
